original_question: Suppose that the polynomial equation F (w0 , w1 , ......, wn ) = 1 defines a smooth affine algebraic hypersurface (these are always parallellizable (Murthy, Swan, n=2; Suslin for general n). Can they be holomorphically immersed in C^n ?
target_in_paper: An unlabeled open problem in arXiv:math/9509202 asking whether a smooth affine algebraic hypersurface of the form F=1, known to be parallelizable, admits a holomorphic immersion into the critical ambient dimension C^n.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the intended geometric class: smooth affine algebraic hypersurfaces given by one polynomial equation F(w_0,\dots,w_n)=1 in C^{n+1}. It also correctly notes the key background fact used to motivate the question, namely that these hypersurfaces are parallelizable (their tangent bundles are trivial), and it asks for the right target phenomenon: existence of a holomorphic immersion into C^n.
missing_details: The base field/analytic ground space should be stated explicitly: everything is over the complex numbers, so X is a complex manifold inside C^{n+1}.
The hypersurface should be named explicitly, e.g. X = {w in C^{n+1} : F(w)=1}.
The smoothness hypothesis should be made stand-alone: dF(w) != 0 for every w in X (equivalently, X is a smooth hypersurface).
The complex dimension should be stated: X has complex dimension n.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether every such smooth hypersurface X admits such an immersion.
The meaning of 'holomorphically immersed' should be made explicit as existence of a holomorphic map f:X->C^n whose differential is injective at every point.
The draft treats parallelizability as parenthetical background; in a stand-alone question it should be clearly marked as motivation rather than as an extra hypothesis.
There are no homogeneity or degree assumptions on F in this problem, so the refined statement should avoid introducing any.
There is no algebraicity requirement on the immersion; the question is about holomorphic immersion, not algebraic immersion.
The draft does not say that the problem is narrowly about hypersurfaces, not more general smooth affine varieties or complete intersections; that scope boundary should be kept explicit.
refined_question: Let F \in C[w_0,\dots,w_n] be a polynomial such that the level hypersurface X = {w \in C^{n+1} : F(w)=1} is smooth, equivalently dF(w) \neq 0 for every w \in X. Then X is a smooth affine algebraic hypersurface of complex dimension n, and its holomorphic tangent bundle is trivial. Must every such X admit a holomorphic immersion f:X \to C^n (that is, a holomorphic map whose differential is injective at every point)?
justification: The arXiv item math/9509202 is a problem list rather than a standard theorem paper, so there is no numbered Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 to target here. Your draft is already very close to the specific hypersurface-level formulation and should not be broadened to the more general neighboring question for arbitrary parallelizable Stein manifolds. The closest verified contextual restatement I could match is Forstneric's later discussion: in §2(6), pp. 151-152, he explicitly says that every closed complex hypersurface in C^{n+1} is parallelizable and that it is unknown whether such hypersurfaces immerse into C^n; in the same discussion he separates this from the broader open problem for all parallelizable Stein manifolds. That confirms that the narrow hypersurface question, not the broader Stein-manifold version, is the paper-faithful target of your draft.
